## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical knowledge of streaming algorithms for frequency analysis—a core skill for systems handling high-volume data streams. It evaluates understanding of the space-accuracy trade-off fundamental to approximate algorithms.

## Key Concepts
- **Misra-Gries sketch**: A deterministic algorithm for finding heavy hitters
- **Heavy hitters**: Elements exceeding a frequency threshold (N/k)
- **Top-K**: Returning the K most frequent elements with approximate counts
- **Batch processing**: Handling grouped updates efficiently
- **Error guarantees**: Bounded recall but possible false positives

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design dynamic range properties with batched updates and amortized analysis, leveraging a segment-tree style approach for real-time run-length maintenance.

## Key Concepts

- Segment tree storing (length, pref1, suf1, best1)
- Merge to propagate cross-boundary runs
- Amortized batch updates vs per-item cost
- Cache-friendly iterative layout

## Code Example

```python
class Node:
    def __init__(self, length=0, pref=0, suf=0, best=0):
        self.length = length
        self.pref = pref
        self.suf = suf
        self.best = best

def merge(a, b):
    length = a.length + b.length
    pref = a.length if a.pref == a.length else a.pref
    if a.pref == a.length:
        pref = a.length + b.pref
    suf = b.length if b.suf == b.length else b.suf
    if b.suf == b.length:
        suf = b.length + a.suf
    best = max(a.best, b.best, a.suf + b.pref)
    return Node(length, pref, suf, best)
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to range flips (set to 0/1) or range updates? 
- How does performance adapt when B approaches n or L is near n?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests distinct counting in streaming with bounded memory, pushing probabilistic data structures and mergeability considerations. HyperLogLog offers scalable accuracy vs memory, a common real-world tradeoff.

## Key Concepts
- Streaming distinct counting
- HyperLogLog, hash distribution, registers
- Mergeability and memory-accuracy tradeoffs

## Code Example
```python
def update(id, M, m_bits):
    h = hash64(id)  # 64-bit hash
    i = h >> (64 - m_bits)
    w = h & ((1 << (64 - m_bits)) - 1)
    rho = 1
    while (w >> (64 - m_bits - rho)) & 1 == 0:
        rho += 1
    M[i] = max(M[i], rho)
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to choose m given a target relative error? 
- How to merge sketches from multiple streams efficiently? 
- What are limitations with very skewed data or hash collisions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to map domain-specific queries to a standard data structure and reason about time/space.

## Key Concepts
- Fenwick Tree (BIT)
- Prefix sums
- Coordinate/value-domain handling

## Code Example
```javascript
class Fenwick {
  constructor(n){ this.n=n; this.f=new Array(n+1).fill(0); }
  add(i, delta){ for(i+=1; i<=this.n; i+= i&-i) this.f[i]+=delta; }
  sum(i){ let s=0; for(i+=1; i>0; i-= i&-i) s+=this.f[i]; return s; }
}
```
